pains.statement: Critical reports and queries take minutes or hours because indexes and access paths were never tuned for today's load.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name a report or screen, typical runtime, and whether ops waits on it daily.

pains.statement: Reads return stale or wrong data because cache layers were bolted on without clear invalidation rules.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Describe a case where users saw wrong balances, counts, or status until a manual refresh.

pains.statement: Nightly batch jobs overlap business hours and lock tables while operators still need the system.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name the job window, what gets locked, and what business process stalls.

pains.statement: Two fields share a name or label but mean different things across modules, causing silent data errors.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Give an example field pair and the downstream report or integration that breaks.

pains.statement: Business logic lives in undocumented stored procedures nobody dares to change.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name a procedure or job and what business rule it encodes that nobody can explain.

pains.statement: Teams export CSVs from green screens or ad-hoc queries because there is no stable read API.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Which workflow exports data manually and how often per week.

pains.statement: A single high-traffic lookup lacks the right index and forces full scans under peak load.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Identify the lookup key, table size, and observed scan vs index behavior.

pains.statement: A mobile or digital initiative is blocked because the legacy core exposes no HTTP APIs.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name the initiative, target channel, and what API or screen access is missing.

pains.statement: Operator workflows still require green-screen or terminal UI that new hires refuse to learn.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name the workflow, headcount affected, and hiring or training friction.

pains.statement: The organization cannot hire or retain maintainers for the dead stack that runs revenue workflows.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Stack name, open reqs, contractor dependence, or last expert departure.

pains.statement: Integrations require manual re-keying between systems because batch files lack stable schemas.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name the systems, file format, and hours spent per week on re-keying.

pains.statement: Audit or compliance needs field lineage and change history the current system cannot produce.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name the audit rule, missing lineage artifact, and last failed or painful audit.

pains.statement: One bounded business module is ready to migrate but leadership fears touching adjacent workflows.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name the module boundary, dependencies, and what makes adjacent areas scary.

pains.statement: Analytics and ops reporting hammer the transactional database because no read path exists.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name reports hitting prod, lock or latency impact, and any rejected replica attempt.

pains.statement: Critical specs live in PDFs, emails, and binders that nobody can search or cite under deadline.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Corpus type, search failure story, and deadline that forced manual archaeology.

pains.statement: Leadership says "we need to modernize" but has no scoped wedge or bounded first deliverable.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Quote the modernization mandate and list stalled initiatives with no owner.

pains.statement: Cutover terror blocks progress — teams fear a one-shot migration will halt operations.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Past failed cutover, rollback story, or explicit "we cannot go down" constraint.

pains.statement: Leadership is blind to operations data trapped in legacy screens and batch outputs.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Decision delayed because data was unavailable or took days to assemble.

pains.statement: Compliance is failing or at risk on an undocumented system with no authoritative data dictionary.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Regulation, finding or near-miss, and artifact auditors asked for but could not get.

pains.statement: Vendor lock-in on legacy runtime or license terms blocks incremental change.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Vendor, contract constraint, and smallest change that was rejected or priced out.

pains.statement: Source code or build artifacts are missing, so changes require reverse engineering or screen scraping.
pains.suggestedEvidence: What is missing, last change attempt, and workaround used today.

pains.statement: A web of point-to-point integrations makes any schema change a multi-team coordination event.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Count integrations, recent schema change delay, and teams involved.
